report.whatTheMapAsked: The 2026-09-02 RESKIN verdict is stale for this arena, exactly as I found on e4-boneyard and e4-dust-flats: since the e4-roads-and-convoys merge, `autoSecureWaveForRun`'s motor clause holds the secure unreachable until `now.motor.objective.arrived`, and on this map the errand is the era's fullest expression yet — a three-stop **deliveries** tour (`objective.kind: "deliveries"`, one Hauler rest at the head of every lease road) threaded through a 30-second weather clock whose every storm **washes out one lease in rotation** (`roads.closed` / `closesNext`, no road bonus and no delivery while it blows). I had to reason about E4's named mechanic continuously and it punished me twice before yielding: my first two rides ran the 36-fuel tank dry (36.0 drawn, north/east undelivered) because multi-leg HAUL chains kept dispatching the 20wu off-road staging legs inside storm phases, where 0.7× movement stretches the same distance to ~1.43× the fuel. The fields that carried it: `now.motor.fuel` (3 tar nodes = 36 lifetime fuel, 24 tank), `roads.corridors/graded/closed`, `weather.phase`+`nextPhaseInSeconds` (the dispatch-timing clock), `vehicle.state/dispatch`, `objective.remaining/delivered`; the verbs: GRADE ×3, HAUL as a staged state machine (home along the old road → walk to the next stake → timed off-road stage leg → road leg out). The winning ride drew 24.7 of 36 fuel purely by dispatching off-road legs only in checked clear windows. That said, the errand was done at t154.9 of 360 — the back half is ordinary fixed-hero stationary survival (fort at the camp stake, seam-chasing economy across 30g-cap seams 40–70wu out, upgrade drafts) wearing the era's dust. Honest verdict for the reskin ladder: the E4 system is load-bearing and here it is finally *scheduling-hard* (fuel × storms × washout rotation is a real planning problem, not a prologue chore), but it still shares the ride with a survival game it doesn't touch.
report.winnability: Winnable through the door from the starting kit, on the third full ride: the survival half is wide (hero never below 100/100 at any view, ended 155.8/175, all works untouched at 334/334, waves 9–12 all "held") but the errand half is genuinely thin — a naive router burns the 36-fuel lifetime tank ~8 fuel short (two honest rides proved it), and the map only opens once hauler legs are dispatched against the published weather clock, one leg per view, off-road staging only in clear windows.
report.lessons:
- e4-gusher-county FIRST SECURE (cold plain boot, w12/360.0s/0g/415 kills/49 calls, hash fnv1a32:f01e0b98, zero defaults, determinism proven by sha256-identical input logs tune-3 vs attempt-1): errand = jiggle-dwell tar (0,-8)→(-12,-8)→GRADE west→hop-HAUL→(12,-8)→GRADE east→(0,8)→GRADE north, then deliveries west→north→east as a ONE-LEG-PER-VIEW state machine; fort = turrets (-3,-6.6),(3,-6.6),(-3,-1) + beacons (0,-1),(-6,-4) at the fixed hero (0,-4); REPAIR_UNDER 55; rig weapon + explicit BLAST_AT at hero feet (threats≥4); 6-pan HARVEST chains scored d_prosp + 0.7×d_camp; errand arrived t154.9 on 24.7/36 fuel.
- THE FUEL-SECONDS LAW, measured: the E4 tank is a LIFETIME 36 (3 nodes × 12), not a rechargeable resource, and storms multiply fuel per wu by ~1.43 (0.7× speed, burn by the second). Two rides died at exactly 36.0 drawn with one lease left. Off-road staging legs between road stakes (20–24wu = 6.7–9.5 fuel) are the whole budget risk: dispatch them ONLY in a checked window (`weather.phase==='clear' && nextPhaseInSeconds+4 > legTime+2.5`, prospector already standing at the stake so walk time is zero). Road legs are storm-tolerant (2.5×speed/0.4×burn makes the tax pennies) — chain those freely.
- MULTI-LEG HAUL CHAINS ARE A FUEL TRAP: each HAUL dispatches at prospector-arrival time, which drifts into storms uncontrollably when three legs share one array. One hauler leg per view, with HOLD-at-the-next-stake as the wait state, made the errand deterministic-cheap (24.7 fuel vs 36.0 twice). The homing chain [HAUL home, mv nextStake, HOLD nextStake] is the exception — homing is a road leg and the pre-walk is free.
- A DEAD ERRAND MUST BE DECLARED DEAD: my errand steps preceded harvest in the array, so when tune-1's hauler stranded dry (drawn=36, stored=0), the generator re-emitted lease walks forever and the prospector commuted instead of panning — income 0.2g/s, mid-game gone. Any errand generator needs a give-up valve (`fuel.drawn≥35.5 && stored<1` → skip errand permanently) even if you believe your fuel discipline.
- The washout rotation (`roads.closed`, one lease per storm, in order) is handled entirely by target-selection at planning time: filter closed, keep a fixed staging-cheap order (west→north→east from the west vehicle spawn), NEVER pre-filter on `closesNext` — it is published even in clear weather and silently flips your route to the expensive staging order. A 12s closure wait costs nothing; 4 extra wu of off-road staging costs 1.3 fuel.
- Deliveries settle themselves: a hauler resting at a washed-out head takes the delivery on reopen; and delivery arrival while the prospector pans 10wu away is fine — the dispatch coordinate is sampled at HAUL time. Pans woven before errand steps in the array (near-pans ≤18wu) turn the west leg into the opening economy (both 30g west seams sit 7–13wu off the west head).
- Survival here is the EASY half (contrast dust-flats): same 1.18× streaming motor_gangs but with 0.4-hp tar sprites padding the packs — 3 turrets + 2 beacons + plating + rig held wave 14 ceiling twice with works at full hp. Don't over-invest in the fort on a deliveries map; invest in the tank.
